# Ecclesiastes Chapter 3 -- Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-12

This log records all verses in Ecclesiastes Chapter 3 where the three translators significantly diverged.

---

## 3:11 — "eternity" vs. "the world" vs. "obscurity" for ha-olam

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-eternity [ha-olam]" | Preserves the Hebrew term with its range of meaning |
| LOGOS | "eternity" | Traditional rendering, captures theological depth |
| PNEUMA | "eternity" | Agrees — the sense of "something beyond" is essential |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** All three converge on "eternity." The alternative "ignorance" (from *'alam*, to hide) is noted but rejected — the sense of longing for the eternal fits the context better.

---

## 3:15 — "God seeks the pursued" vs. "God seeks what has been driven away"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "God seeks the-pursued [et-nirdaf]" | Literal |
| LOGOS | "God seeks what has been driven away" | Formal equivalent |
| PNEUMA | "God makes the same things happen over and over" | Interpretive paraphrase |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "God seeks what has been driven away" (LOGOS). Preserves the ambiguity without collapsing it into a single interpretation.

---

## 3:18 — "testing them" vs. "tests people" vs. "the human condition"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "God is-testing-them [le-varam]" | Literal — *barar* means to purify/test |
| LOGOS | "God is testing them" | Direct formal equivalent |
| PNEUMA | "how God tests people so they can see" | Adds interpretive clarity |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "God is testing them" (LOGOS/EMET). The Hebrew *le-varam* does mean "to test/purify them." PNEUMA's expansion is helpful but unnecessary in the text itself.

**Status:** All resolved.
